transcript:
Meeting header: 2028-07-16 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Maya, Jonas, Laura, Ravi, Diane

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya Patel, account exec at Redwood Inference. We'll run through a hosted API demo — embeddings + reranking — and show our Console Optimize hints. Jonas from the SE team is with me.
[00:20] Jonas: Hi all, quick agenda — architecture, live demo against Hightide sample docs, rerank tuning, then Q&A.
[00:35] Laura: Sounds good. We're mainly evaluating hosted first, we might go dedicated later, want to see the integration effort.
[00:45] Jonas: Great. So high level: two endpoints you'll call — /embeddings.v1 to vectorize content and /rerank.v1 which scores candidates given a query. Both are available on the hosted API, SDKs, and Console shows examples. We'll demo with your product catalog sample.
[01:05] Ravi: Quick question — how much control do we have over the reranker features? We have signals like click-through and CTR history.
[01:12] Jonas: The hosted reranker accepts additional feature vectors as metadata — you can pass numeric features per document. We also support custom feature weights in the rerank config or you can run a lightweight on-top model in your infra.
[01:30] Diane: OK, and what about latency? Our SLA target is sub-120ms 95th for product search.
[01:38] Maya: Good Q. For hosted we show typical latency profiles per model in the Console. For small-to-mid doc sizes we regularly hit 40-80ms for embedding + candidate scoring in many cases; depends on batch size and your window. If you need lower, Dedicated pools or colocated routing help.
[01:55] Jonas: I'll show a benchmark in a minute. Note that our auto-batching and prefix caching reduce per-token cost and the KV cache helps for session-y use.
[02:10] Jonas: Switching to demo — I'm in the Console, opening the Hightide demo project. Deck and dataset link in chat: https://redwood.example.com/decks/hightide-demo and sample corpus: https://drive.example.com/hightide-sample.csv
[02:35] Jonas: First, embeddings call — POST /v1/embeddings with text block. Response returns a 512-d float vector (we also support 768/1024 dims depending on model). Slight hiccup in transcript: the model is Redwood-vector-2 but docs sometimes show vector-two, small naming drift in older docs.
[03:05] Jonas: Now candidate generation: we recommend standard vector nearest-neighbors (we have FAISS-based nearest service) then rerank top-K using /v1/rerank. Rerank takes the query, list of candidate ids, optional per-candidate metadata and returns a ranked list with scores.
[03:35] Laura: Do we have to host an index ourselves? We have a managed Elastic + vector plugin today.
[03:42] Jonas: You can keep your index and call our rerank endpoint with the top-K results; no need to move your index. Many customers do that to keep control over sharding and existing infra. If you want a fully-hosted pipeline, Redwood Dedicated can host the index too.
[04:00] Ravi: Regarding feature tying, can we pass CTR and recency and have the reranker learn from it?
[04:07] Jonas: For hosted rerank we don't train on your features live; you pass features and specify a deterministic scoring config or a linear weight blend. We also provide a managed reweighter in Optimize that suggests weights based on held-out queries — not learning user PII or storing signals without permission. For advanced custom models, we support bringing your own ranker and we run A/B routing.
[04:35] Diane: Security — we need SOC2, encryption keys, audit logs and SSO.
[04:42] Maya: We're SOC2 Type II, integrate with customer KMS for Private deployments, and Console has audit trails per-token and per-route. I'll attach the security pack after the call.
[04:55] Jonas: There's a small note — hosted does not yet support customer-managed HSM for the shared plan; that's available on Private deployments.
[05:05] Laura: Understood. Can you show a rerank tuning example?
[05:10] Jonas: Sure. Loading our sample search page. Here's a query "waterproof hiking jacket". Baseline vector retrieval returns ten candidates. We call rerank with the query, title, description, CTR, and in-stock flag.
[05:30] Jonas: [shows request body snippet] You can see each candidate has a features array like {"ctr": 0.12, "recency_days": 14, "in_stock": 1}. Note: transcript JSONs sometimes replace braces — but request format in docs is clear.
[05:50] Jonas: We run rerank and get reordered results — items with better CTR and recency bubble up even if semantic relevance was slightly lower. You can toggle the weight of CTR in the Console slider to see live changes.
[06:10] Laura: That's neat. For our catalog, title length varies a lot — does embedding model handle that?
[06:18] Jonas: Yes, the embedding model normalization helps. We also recommend storing precomputed embeddings for titles and descriptions in your index. For long product descriptions, we chunk. There's also guidance in Optimize: use 256-d title vectors + 512-d desc vectors, fuse them in rerank features.
[06:40] Ravi: Any examples of cost numbers? We're sensitive to per-token + per-query costs at scale.
[06:46] Maya: Pricing is usage-based: per-embedding unit and per-rerank call. Optimize will recommend batching and quantized models if cost-sensitive. For example, switching from full float 1024-d to 8-bit quantized 512-d reduces cost ~3-4x with small drop in relevance — the Console shows expected metric delta. We'll include a cost-projection sheet.
[07:10] Diane: Quantization — will that affect embeddings drift? We can't accept big relevance regressions.
[07:16] Jonas: There's always a tradeoff. Optimize can run small evals on your labeled queries to estimate lift/regress. We recommend a canary rollout and guard rails with automatic fallback to float model if quality dips.
[07:35] Jonas: Quick demo of Console Optimize: it scanned our sample runs and recommended a quantization profile + batch size 16 for your expected QPS. It also suggested rerank weight 0.25 for CTR and 0.15 for recency to maximize NDCG on your sample.
[08:00] Laura: How do we validate that on our prod traffic? Can we run an A/B test?
[08:06] Maya: Yes, we support canary/AB policies in the Console. You can route X% of traffic to the new rerank config and collect metrics. We'll provide the evaluation harness and a sample query set.
[08:25] Ravi: About data retention — do you store our queries or embeddings?
[08:30] Maya: By default hosted keeps logs for 30 days for debugging unless you opt in for longer. You can request no retention or token-level redaction. Private deployments give you full control. We'll include the retention options in the security doc.
[08:48] Diane: For compliance we need IP allowlist and VPC peering.
[08:52] Jonas: VPC peering is available for Private and some Dedicated setups; IP allowlist is part of the hosted enterprise plan.
[09:00] Jonas: Now I'll run a quick benchmark — I'm going to send 100 sample queries in a small runner to measure embedding + rerank 95th latency. Running...
[09:15] Jonas: Results: median 62ms, p95 118ms for this workload (note: synthetic test on a small sample). I'll upload raw output to the shared drive.
[09:30] Laura: Nice, that's promising. What about throughput limits?
[09:34] Jonas: Hosted has per-account QPS soft limits which we can raise; Dedicated provides guaranteed capacity with autoscaling.
[09:42] Diane: Integrations — our stack uses Node + Python microservices. SDKs?
[09:47] Maya: SDKs for both, example code in the Console, and quickstart templates. We'll send a Node example that shows embedding + rerank call flow.
[10:00] Ravi: Any gotchas with tokenization or weird model output?
[10:05] Jonas: For embeddings it's straightforward, just plain text. For rerank, ensure you normalize casing and strip HTML; we provide client helpers. Also watch out for synonyms — Optimize can suggest query rewrites for common phrase variants.
[10:25] Laura: What if we want more control over training the reranker?
[10:29] Jonas: You can train a custom ranker on your side and run it as the final stage after our rerank or replace our reranker entirely; we support BYO-model routing. Many customers use our rerank for quick wins and then graduate to a tailored model.
[10:45] Diane: Next steps recap?
[10:48] Maya: Recap — we'll provision a 30-day hosted trial and API key, Jonas will run the benchmark and share results, you (Laura) will send labeled queries, and we'll schedule a follow-up check-in after you've run the runner.
[11:05] Laura: OK sounds good. Can you also include a sample cost projection and sample Node/Python snippets?
[11:10] Maya: Yes — will share both and the security pack.
[11:15] Jonas: Anything else on the technical side?
[11:18] Ravi: One last thing — how does caching work with rerank? If same query repeats, will cached embedding help?
[11:25] Jonas: We do prefix and KV caching for repeated contexts; for pure query repeats you can cache the embedding result client-side or use our prefix cache to avoid recompute. The rerank still scores top-K but with cached embeddings cost goes down.
[11:40] Diane: Thanks, this was useful.
[11:43] Maya: Thanks everyone — I'll follow up with notes and links. Links again: demo deck and sample corpus in chat.
[11:50] End meeting.
